page: Amazon Web Services c9g.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 silicon clocked at 3.3 GHz. The hardware layout consists of 48 dedicated physical cores mapped to 48 vCPUs with a single thread per core, avoiding virtualization resource contention. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 96.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation that matches the resource density of compute-heavy architectural requirements. Network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps, while local instance storage and GPU accelerators are absent.

Benchmark evaluations place the platform in the upper deciles for CPU throughput and system responsiveness. In synthetic compute benchmarks, the instance recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 2,387.0 and a multi-core score of 28,306.0, supported by a Clang software compilation score of 91,952.0. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 36.47 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 623.71 GB/sec. Memory subsystems demonstrate high throughput, registering 188.26 GB/sec in uncached 256MB read operations, a PassMark memory score of 4,684.89, and a database operations index of 47,370.83. Concurrency benchmarks show 136.88 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 103.35 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The absence of hyperthreading delivers predictable per-core execution, though software pipelines must be targeted to the arm64 architecture. Without integrated local NVMe storage, workloads rely strictly on remote block volumes over the 25 Gbps network interface. Given its high core count, high memory bandwidth, and 2.0 GB per core balance, the instance is suited for parallel software builds, continuous integration pipelines, batch computing, high-traffic static web servers, and distributed in-memory cache tiers.

Configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs with one thread per core and 96.0 GB of memory, it delivers a 2.0 GB per core ratio tailored for CPU-intensive processing. The instance includes a 25 Gbps baseline network interface, while omitting bundled local storage and GPU hardware. Benchmark testing demonstrates upper-decile multi-core performance, recording 28,306.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 91,952.0 in Clang software compilation, and 136.88 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. Memory throughput remains robust with 188.26 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Due to its dedicated physical core layout and high processing density, the c9g.12xlarge is suited for software build pipelines, distributed web architectures, high-throughput caching, and batch data processing.
